result: His example is false. Ordinary cusp: affine A = C[t^2,t^3] = C[x,y]/(y^2-x^3) is weighted homogeneous (weights 2,3); E = 2x d/dx + 3y d/dy is a derivation of A, L_E = d i_E + i_E d is multiplication by the weight, all forms of positive degree have positive weight, so the Kahler de Rham cohomology is C in degree 0 = b of the cusp. Projective cuspidal cubic: same homotopy on convergent series gives the analytic Poincare lemma at the cusp, GAGA gives H^1 = H^1(S^2) = 0; check chi(O)-chi(Omega^1)+chi(Omega^2) = 0-0+2 = 2 = chi(S^2) (torsion of Omega^1 has length tau = 2; Omega^2 = C[x]/(x^2)). The node xy = 0 is homogeneous too. Refined: the naive complex fails at non-quasi-homogeneous singularities (K. Saito 1971, locator unverified), e.g. the unibranch x^4+y^5+x^2y^3 = 0; his struck first wording 'singulière (disons unibranche si on y tient)' was right.
